- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes too early; add a 5–15% downward bias to early forecast peaks.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 2x prior peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 5–10% downward revision in next 7-day forecast.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops below 1.00 within 10 days), model tends to overpredict; apply a “reversion buffer” rule: cap forecast at 1.2x recent 7-day low.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “neutral” (0.00) or “flat” periods, model often underperforms; increase forecast baseline by 5–10% to account for low volatility bias.
